body.text: Which baseline blood tests, ECGs and imaging save time upon arrival?

Bringing recent baseline diagnostics—typically completed within 30 to 90 days of travel—lets your receiving physician review existing markers immediately rather than starting from zero. While Turkish hospitals routinely repeat key pre-operative labs on site for legal and safety compliance, prior blood panels, ECGs, and original imaging files prevent unnecessary scheduling delays and repeated specialist consultations.
Ask your home clinic for digital exports plus one printed summary, requesting raw DICOM files on a USB drive rather than screen photos.

body.text: Even with a complete file, your treating hospital in Türkiye will decide which tests must be repeated locally before any procedure. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
How should you translate and carry chronic medication lists?

List every regular prescription, over-the-counter drug, and supplement using its international generic (INN) name alongside exact milligram strength, daily schedule, and prescribing reason. Brand names vary widely between countries, so generic names allow Turkish doctors, pharmacists, and customs officers to verify your regimen instantly without translation errors or dosing confusion.

Under [Turkish Ministry of Trade passenger customs guidance](https://ticaret.gov.tr/gumruk-islemleri/sikca-sorulan-sorular/english/passenger-transactions), travellers may bring personal-use medicines in quantities matching their stay when supported by a doctor's report or prescription. The [UK FCDO Turkey health guidance](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health) also notes that controlled substances—such as strong opioid painkillers, sedatives, or ADHD stimulants—require checking with a Turkish embassy before flying.

items: Pack essential medicines in hand luggage in original pharmacy-labelled boxes.
Carry a signed English doctor's letter listing your name, generic drugs, doses, and needles or devices.
Bring your trip supply plus a three-to-five-day delay buffer.
Add a Turkish-English allergy line (e.g., Penisilin Alerjisi for penicillin).

body.text: Why does ITO advise against sending sensitive records in an unverified first message?

Sending passport scans, full diagnostic histories, or clinical photos in an initial contact form or unencrypted messaging chat exposes highly sensitive personal data before you have verified who is receiving it. Under Türkiye's [Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK)](https://www.kvkk.gov.tr/Icerik/6649/Personal-Data-Protection-Law), health records are special-category data requiring strict confidentiality and explicit consent controls.

At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about), our two founders operate as an independent, client-paid, flat-fee advisory—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions. In a first conversation about our [medical tourism coordination services](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism), we only need your planned dates, preferred city, general specialty area, and mobility or lodging needs. Once you independently select a licensed hospital, you transfer clinical files directly through that hospital's official patient portal or encrypted intake channel.
What emergency contact card should you carry in Istanbul?

Keep a printed, wallet-sized bilingual card in your coat pocket and phone case so a hotel receptionist, driver, or paramedic can act within seconds if you feel unwell. Relying solely on a locked smartphone battery fails when you need urgent help, especially during post-procedure recovery or across language barriers in Istanbul.

In Türkiye, 112 is the unified national emergency number for ambulance, police, and fire. The [Turkish Ministry of Health International Patient Assistance Unit](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN%2C69450/0-850-288-38-38-international-patient-assistance-unit-interpreting-and-call-center-continues-service.html) also operates a 24/7 six-language interpreting line (+90 850 288 38 38) that supports foreign callers contacting 112 or the 184 SABİM health line.

faq.q: How recent should baseline blood tests be for a medical trip to Türkiye?
faq.a: Aim for labs and ECGs dated within 30 to 90 days of arrival. Turkish hospitals typically repeat pre-operative blood work on site, but recent baselines help specialists plan faster.

faq.q: Do I need a notarized Turkish translation of my medical records?
faq.a: Major Istanbul international hospitals accept clear English summaries and lab reports. Notarized Turkish translations are rarely needed, though a bilingual allergy and medication line helps at pharmacies.

faq.q: Can I bring prescription painkillers or insulin into Türkiye?
faq.a: Personal-use prescription medicines and insulin are generally permitted in hand luggage with original pharmacy packaging, prescriptions, and a signed doctor's letter. For controlled medications such as opioids, sedatives, or stimulants, confirm current import rules with the Turkish embassy before departure.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye review my medical scans or recommend treatments?
faq.a: No. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. Itinerary of Türkiye is a client-paid, flat-fee travel and logistics advisory and does not provide medical advice or take commissions from clinics.

faq.q: Should I carry DICOM scans on a USB drive or print X-ray films?
faq.a: Carry raw DICOM files on a USB drive plus the written radiologist report. Physicians prefer DICOM data so they can measure slices accurately on hospital workstations.

faq.q: What number do I call for an ambulance in Istanbul if I do not speak Turkish?
faq.a: Dial 112 for any emergency in Türkiye, say 'English' clearly, and state your address. The Ministry of Health's 24/7 line (+90 850 288 38 38) provides live interpreting.
